title: Narrowband searches for continuous gravitational waves from known pulsars in the first two parts of the fourth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA observing run
extended_summary:
This paper is not an education study and does not examine ChatGPT or any mathematics intervention in grades 6–8. Instead, it reports an astrophysics analysis of narrowband searches for continuous gravitational waves from known pulsars during the first two parts of the fourth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA observing run. The work addresses the question of whether targeted searches of pulsars can detect or constrain continuous gravitational-wave emission using data from the LVK detectors.

The approach is an observational data-analysis study using gravitational-wave detector data, not an educational intervention. The paper describes search methods, candidate pulsar targets, and analysis results from the observing run, with emphasis on astrophysical signal characterization and upper limits / constraints rather than human participants or instructional outcomes. No educational population, user group, school setting, or comparator condition is present.

Because the paper is outside the requested topic, there is no directly empirical ChatGPT mathematics intervention evidence to extract. The closest comparator evidence is also absent in the sense relevant to the search: this paper does not provide any educational intervention, classroom implementation, or control group comparison. It should be treated as irrelevant to the target question rather than as supporting evidence for it.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is an astrophysics paper on gravitational-wave searches, not an education or AI-in-education study. There is no empirical educational intervention, counterfactual design, or student outcome methodology to evaluate.
